nv_urban_crag.blurb: Urban Crag is a limestone sport crag on the east flank of Lone Mountain, a small hill ringed by suburbs on the northwest side of the Las Vegas valley. Nineteen sport routes climb a big cave-like recess, from an easy 5.5 through a spread of 5.8s and 5.10s up to a handful of 5.11s and 5.12s, so the grades lean toward intermediate and harder. The wall runs from vertical to mildly overhanging and faces east, which gives morning sun and afternoon shade. It is a short walk from town, sheltered, and a handy fallback on cold days or when the sandstone at Red Rock is wet.
nv_urban_crag.parking_note: Leave the car at the neighbourhood park at the end of Jensen, on the north side of the hill, then pick up the trail that heads south.

nv_angel_food_wall.blurb: Angel Food Wall is a sandstone face in the White Rock Spring corner of Red Rock Canyon, west of Las Vegas. It holds nineteen trad routes, mostly moderate multi-pitch lines on a wall of about 500 feet, with the bulk of the grades falling between 5.6 and 5.9 and just one or two at 5.10 and 5.11. The face looks northeast and stays shaded until around midday, which suits warm days. Expect a trail-and-wash approach with a bit of scrambling, and easy walk-off options down a gully behind the wall. Good for parties stepping up to longer climbs.

nv_watchtower_2.blurb: The Watchtower is a sandstone sport wall in the Calico I (First Pullout) part of Red Rock, outside Las Vegas. It forms the biggest cluster in a small group of walls that also includes an alcove, the Lone Pine Wall and The Chasm. All nineteen routes are bolted, with the heaviest concentrations at 5.8 and 5.11 and a few at 5.12. The hike in leaves the First Pullout and goes up a slot beyond Civilization Crag, over a gully and up to the base, taking roughly twenty minutes at an easy pace. Cacti surround the base, and a helmet is a sensible addition.

nv_left_side.blurb: Left Side is the western section of the Universal Wall, a large limestone face above the Mary Jane Falls trailhead in the Spring Mountains near Mount Charleston. It holds nineteen routes, mostly sport with two trad lines, and combines short climbs at the base with a few long multi-pitch lines. Grades run from 5.5 up to 5.13, with a big middle band of 5.9 and 5.10. The rock is generally sound but there are loose patches and hollow flakes, and falling rock is a real concern when parties are stacked above you. This section stays shaded for most of the day and can feel cold.

nv_sunny_and_steep.blurb: Sunny and Steep is a steep sandstone sport crag on the far side of Kraft Mountain in Calico Basin, Red Rock. Nineteen bolted routes of roughly 40 to 100 feet are concentrated at the hard end: about half are 5.12, with a few 5.11s and only a couple of easier lines near 5.8 and 5.9. The climbing is overhanging and powerful, the bolts are glue-ins, and a flat terrace sits below the wall. It catches sun from mid-morning until dusk. The walk in is long by Red Rock standards, about 30 to 60 minutes from the Kraft Mountain lot, by either the west or east loop.

nv_main_rock_2.blurb: Main Rock is the principal wall of Spooner Crag, tucked in the trees on Lake Tahoe's Nevada east shore just above the junction of Highways 28 and 50. Nineteen routes, almost all bolted with one trad line, run from about 5.8 to 5.13, with the weight in the 5.10 to 5.12 range. Climbs are mostly single pitch, with a couple of two-pitch options, and the style is steep and edgy, with overhanging moves on a number of lines. It sits at a modest elevation for the Tahoe area, so it can be climbed through much of the year. The roadside parking lot makes it a quick afternoon outing.
